## Definition

**Correlation** measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two variables. It tells us how much one variable tends to change when the other changes.

## The Correlation Coefficient

Denoted as **r** (sample) or **ρ** (rho, population), the correlation coefficient ranges from -1 to +1.

| Value | Interpretation |
|-------|----------------|
| r = +1 | Perfect positive correlation |
| r = 0 | No linear correlation |
| r = -1 | Perfect negative correlation |

## Direction of Correlation

| Type | Description | Example |
|------|-------------|---------|
| Positive | Both variables increase together | Height and weight |
| Negative | One increases, other decreases | Age and reaction time |
| Zero | No systematic relationship | Shoe size and IQ |

## Strength Guidelines

| r value | Interpretation |
|---------|----------------|
| .00 - .10 | Negligible |
| .10 - .30 | Small/weak |
| .30 - .50 | Medium/moderate |
| .50 - .70 | Large/strong |
| .70 - 1.0 | Very strong |

## Visual Representation

```
Strong Positive (r ≈ .8)    No Correlation (r ≈ 0)    Strong Negative (r ≈ -.8)
        ●                         ●  ●                        ●
       ●                       ●     ●                         ●
      ●                     ●   ●   ●                           ●
     ●                       ● ●  ●                              ●
    ●                      ●    ●                                 ●
```

## Types of Correlation Tests

| Test | When to Use |
|------|-------------|
| Pearson's r | Interval/ratio data, linear relationship |
| Spearman's rho | Ordinal data, or non-linear monotonic |

## Correlation ≠ Causation

**Critical concept:** Correlation does not imply causation.

```
A and B are correlated:

Possible explanations:
1. A causes B        A → B
2. B causes A        B → A
3. C causes both     C → A, C → B
4. Coincidence       No causal link
```

## R Code Example

```r
# Pearson correlation
cor.test(x, y)

# Spearman correlation
cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman")

# Correlation matrix
cor(data_frame)
```

## Reporting (APA Style)

> There was a significant positive correlation between study hours and exam scores, *r*(48) = .65, *p* < .001.
